title: The tensor product of commutative algebras is their pushout
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$, $B$ commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and let $A\otimes_RB$ be the tensor product of the $R$-modules $A$ and $B$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. (1) There is a unique multiplication on $A\otimes_RB$ with $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$ making it a commutative ring with unit $1\otimes1$; with the structure map $r\mapsto r\cdot(1\otimes1)$ it is an $R$-algebra, and $\iota_A:A\to A\otimes_RB$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, and $\iota_B:B\to A\otimes_RB$, $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras. (2) For every commutative $R$-algebra $C$ and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $f:A\to C$, $g:B\to C$ there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $h:A\otimes_RB\to C$ with $h(a\otimes b)=f(a)g(b)$ for all $a\in A$, $b\in B$; in particular $h\circ\iota_A=f$ and $h\circ\iota_B=g$. (3) Two homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $h_1,h_2:A\otimes_RB\to C$ with $h_1\circ\iota_A=h_2\circ\iota_A$ and $h_1\circ\iota_B=h_2\circ\iota_B$ are equal.
